chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sabbah al-Hazza', from Abu Asama, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and a man from the Mugheira clan asked him about something from the Sunnah. He said: 'There is nothing that anyone from the children of Adam needs except that a Sunnah has flowed regarding it from Allah and from His Messenger; he who recognizes it recognizes it, and he who denies it denies it.'

The man said, 'So what is the Sunnah regarding entering the toilet?' He said: 'Remember Allah and seek refuge with Allah from the Satan, the Pelted one. And when you are finished, say: 'All praise is for Allah upon what He removed from me of harm, in ease and health.'

The man said, 'So if a person is in that state and cannot be patient until he looks at what comes out of him?' He said: 'There is no human on earth except that two angels are assigned to him. So when he is in that state, they bend his neck, then they say: 'O son of Adam! Look at what you were toiling for in the world, to what it has become.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and etiquettes for using the toilet in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the comprehensive nature of divine Sunnah, extending even to mundane acts like using the toilet, where remembrance of Allah and seeking refuge from Satan transform daily routines into worship. It highlights the Shia belief in the constant presence of two angels who monitor human conduct, using the act of looking at excrement as a metaphor for reflecting on the transient nature of worldly labor and the inevitability of death.
